title: Wait times are the top theme across 4 of 6 resident surveys
description: Reading across six resident-experience surveys on four platforms, wait times are cited in 41% of open-text responses and lead the themes in four of them. The pattern holds across different authors and different instruments, which is what makes it structural rather than an artefact of one survey's wording.
data_note: Illustrative. Theme frequencies, satisfaction scores and platform mix are fabricated for demonstration.

confidence.rationale: Theme extraction reconciles across four platforms after de-duplicating respondents who answered more than one survey. Held below 100 because two surveys use different open-text prompts, so the denominators are not perfectly comparable.

action: Break the theme down by region, then brief leadership.
source_text: Open-text theme extraction across six surveys and four platforms.

title: Western region is a 58% outlier on wait-time complaints
description: Western sits at 58% against Central 39%, Eastern 31% and Northern 28% — nineteen points clear of the next region and nearly double the lowest. The concentration is what turns a portfolio-wide theme into something with an address on it.
data_note: Illustrative. Regional splits are fabricated for demonstration and do not describe real Maryland service-center performance.

confidence.rationale: Region is derived from the respondent's ZIP, which about 6% of responses leave blank; those are excluded rather than imputed. The ranking is stable under that exclusion, the exact percentages less so.

action: Pull Western-region verbatims, then recommend a service-center review.
source_text: ZIP-derived region joined to service-center visit logs.

title: Permit Satisfaction Survey — 22 responses from one IP range
description: Twenty-two responses, 11% of that survey, arrived from a single IP range inside a 40-minute window. That is what group completion at a service center looks like, and it is also what bot traffic looks like. Excluding them moves the survey's satisfaction score by about three points, so I have not.
data_note: Illustrative. The flagged survey, its response counts and the submission pattern are fabricated for demonstration.

confidence.rationale: Deliberately below the action threshold. The submission pattern is real and reproducible; its INTERPRETATION is genuinely ambiguous, and a shared IP range is expected behaviour at a public terminal. Held for a human rather than resolved automatically.

action: Decide whether to keep and flag these responses, or exclude them.
